messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8924257/
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41378-022-00357-3

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Droplet-Based Digital Microfluidic CRISPR/Cas9-MAGE (CRMAGE) Recombineering for Automated Bacterial Strain Engineering (galK Disruption and Indigoidine Pathway Optimization in E. coli)

REAGENTS USED:
  - gRNA Plasmid (pMAZ-SK, curable CRISPR/Cas9 guide-RNA plasmid, 100-200 ng per reaction)
  - 70 bp Mutagenic Oligo (single-stranded recombineering oligo, 0.5 uL of 10 pmol/uL stock per reaction)
  - Electrocompetent E. coli Cells (MG1655/MG1616-derived, 50 uL per reaction)
  - Recovery Medium (Lennox LB with 100 ug/mL carbenicillin and 35 ug/mL chloramphenicol, 1 mL per reaction)
  - Kanamycin Selection Reagent (50 ug/mL final concentration, added post-recovery)
  - Anhydrotetracycline (aTet, 200 ng/mL, Cas9 induction/counter-selection reagent)
  - Galactose MacConkey Indicator Medium (1% galactose agar, colorimetric galK screen)
  - IPTG Induction Reagent (isopropyl beta-D-1-thiogalactopyranoside, indigoidine pathway induction)

STEPS:
1. Droplet loading: dispense gRNA plasmid, 70 bp oligo, and electrocompetent cell droplets (nanoliter-scale acoustic-printer droplets) into individually addressable chip wells via a Labcyte Echo 550 acoustic liquid handler.
2. On-chip mixing: actuate electrowetting (AC, 80-100 kHz, 10-100 ms pulse) to merge the plasmid, oligo, and cell droplets within each of the 100 individually addressable reaction chambers.
3. Electroporation: apply an exponential-decay voltage pulse across each chamber's electrode pair (60 V optimal for 20 um electrode gap, 100 V optimal for 100 um gap) to transform the merged droplet.
4. Recovery: incubate the transformed droplet in recovery medium for 2 h at 37 C.
5. Selection: add kanamycin and incubate 3 h at 37 C to select for cells retaining the CRISPR-MAGE plasmids.
6. Induction/counter-selection: add anhydrotetracycline and incubate overnight (~12 h) at 37 C to induce Cas9 expression, which counter-selects against unedited wild-type cells.
7. galK disruption screen: plate a recovered aliquot on 1% galactose MacConkey agar; galK-disrupted (mutant) colonies appear white while wild-type colonies ferment galactose and appear red, giving a colorimetric readout of editing success.
8. Indigoidine pathway optimization: for each of 6 gRNA/oligo target sets (2 targeting the bpsA/sfp promoter, 4 targeting the native glnA promoter), repeat steps 1-6, then add IPTG and incubate at 30 C to induce indigoidine biosynthesis.
9. Detection: quantify GFP-based transformation efficiency (excitation/emission 460 nm/515-535 nm) as a process-validation readout across the 100 parallel reactions, and quantify indigoidine yield per mutant strain by absorbance at 615 nm normalized to 800 nm background; discard analyzed droplets after measurement.

INTERPRETATION: Successful on-chip CRMAGE is confirmed by a galK wild-type-killing (disruption) rate statistically indistinguishable from benchtop CRMAGE (98+-3% on-chip, N=16, vs. 94+-5% benchtop, N=6), by over 80% successful GFP transformation across 100 parallel electroporation reactions, and by measurable increases in indigoidine absorbance for glnA-targeted mutants (e.g., glnA-40) relative to the unmutated control, supporting use of the platform for scalable, automated, combinatorial genetic pathway engineering.

module fluorescence

manifest grna_plasmid
manifest oligo_dna
manifest competent_cells
manifest recovery_medium
manifest kanamycin
manifest anhydrotetracycline
manifest iptg
manifest galactose_media

instructions:

repeat 10 times {
    plasmid = dispense 10 units of grna_plasmid
    oligo = dispense 5 units of oligo_dna
    cells = dispense 50 units of competent_cells

    mix1 = mix plasmid with oligo for 10s
    edited = mix mix1 with cells for 60s

    medium = dispense 100 units of recovery_medium
    recovered = mix edited with medium for 30s
    heat recovered at 37c for 120m

    kan = dispense 20 units of kanamycin
    selected = mix recovered with kan for 30s
    heat selected at 37c for 180m

    atet = dispense 10 units of anhydrotetracycline
    induced = mix selected with atet for 30s
    heat induced at 37c for 720m

    efficiency = detect fluorescence on induced for 30s

    if (efficiency < 80) {
        dispose induced
    }
}

media = dispense 50 units of galactose_media
plasmid2 = dispense 10 units of grna_plasmid
oligo2 = dispense 5 units of oligo_dna
cells2 = dispense 50 units of competent_cells

mixA = mix plasmid2 with oligo2 for 10s
mixB = mix mixA with cells2 for 60s
screened = mix mixB with media for 60s
heat screened at 37c for 720m

colony_color = detect fluorescence on screened for 60s

if (colony_color >= 90) {
    dispose screened
}

repeat 6 times {
    plasmid3 = dispense 10 units of grna_plasmid
    oligo3 = dispense 5 units of oligo_dna
    cells3 = dispense 50 units of competent_cells

    mixC = mix plasmid3 with oligo3 for 10s
    mixD = mix mixC with cells3 for 60s

    medium2 = dispense 100 units of recovery_medium
    recovered2 = mix mixD with medium2 for 30s
    heat recovered2 at 37c for 120m

    inducer = dispense 10 units of iptg
    production = mix recovered2 with inducer for 30s
    heat production at 30c for 720m

    absorbance615 = detect fluorescence on production for 30s

    if (absorbance615 < 60) {
        dispose production
    }
}

numeric_mismatches.note: The paper's chip performs up to 100 genetic modification reactions in parallel across a 10x10 individually addressable electrode array. The BioScript loop uses 10 iterations as a representative subset rather than a literal 1:1 scaling of the 100-chamber array.

BioScript has no primitive for an applied voltage/electric-field pulse. The paper's exponential-decay electroporation pulse (60-100 V) is represented by the 'edited = mix mix1 with cells' step, since droplet merging (electrowetting) and electroporation occur at the same electrode pair immediately in sequence.

BioScript exposes only one generic detect module. It is reused here to represent GFP fluorescence (an actual fluorescence signal), the MacConkey red/white colorimetric galK screen (not fluorescence), and the 615 nm/800 nm absorbance ratio for indigoidine quantification (not fluorescence), since no dedicated colorimetric/absorbance detect module exists in the grammar.

These pass/fail cutoffs are illustrative approximations of the paper's reported success rates (>80% GFP transformation, ~98% galK killing rate) rather than literal numeric thresholds stated in the source text; the paper does not specify a numeric indigoidine absorbance cutoff, so 60 is an authored placeholder.

numeric_mismatches.field: individually addressable 100-well chip topology, acoustic-printer droplet volumes (nL scale), Table 1 arcing/failure comparison, Sanger sequencing verification (Fig. 3c, Supp. Fig. 5)
